letters.title: Cover letter
letters.why: One page that tells the officer who you are, why France, where you will live, how you support yourself and what you will do with your time.
guidance: Every figure and date must agree with the documents behind it: the same address as your accommodation proof, the same income as your statements.
US consulates accept English. A short French version alongside is a courtesy, not a requirement.
One letter covers you both. Each adult still signs their own application form.
If your income is close to the benchmark, the letter is where you explain your budget and your savings.
Sign and date it by hand after printing.

letters.title: Declaration not to work
letters.why: The visitor route requires each adult to sign an attestation sur l'honneur that they will not work in France. French with an English translation below.
guidance: Each adult signs their own. Sign and date it by hand after printing.
Working for a French employer or French clients is not allowed on this visa.

letters.title: Declaration not to work · Sam
letters.why: The visitor route requires each adult to sign an attestation sur l'honneur that they will not work in France. French with an English translation below.
guidance: Each adult signs their own. Sign and date it by hand after printing.
Working for a French employer or French clients is not allowed on this visa.

letters.title: Statement of resources
letters.why: A one-page table of your monthly income and savings, matching the statements in your file. Officers read hundreds of files; a summary that matches gets read.
guidance: Consulates benchmark resources against the French net minimum wage, €1,477.93 a month since 1 June 2026, per adult. It is a benchmark, not a fixed legal floor, and each consulate applies its own standard.
Many applicants show more than the benchmark in income, or about a year of it in savings, so nobody has to ask.
Attach three months of statements for every account listed, and the proof of each income source.
Use one exchange rate for the whole file and say which.

letters.title: Host's attestation d'hébergement
letters.why: Only if you will stay with someone at first. Your host signs that you will live with them; it stands in for a lease as your proof of accommodation.
guidance: Your host signs and dates it and attaches a copy of their ID and a recent proof of their address, such as a utility bill or the deed.
This is a letter from your host, not the mairie's attestation d'accueil, which is for short visits of under three months.
The address must match the one in your cover letter.

cover-letter.title: Cover letter
cover-letter.text:
Jordan Ellis
123 Sample Street
Asheville, NC 28801
jordan@example.com

12 September 2026

Consulate General of France in Atlanta
Visa Section

## Re: Application for a long-stay visitor visa (VLS-TS « visiteur »), passport no. X0000000

Dear Sir or Madam,

My spouse, Sam Ellis, and I are applying for a long-stay visitor visa (VLS-TS « visiteur ») to live in France from 15 February 2027, for one year, renewable.

We are retired and wish to spend this part of our lives in France. We plan to take French classes, walk and cycle the Gironde, volunteer with a local community garden, and have our grown children visit.

We will live at Furnished rental, 8 rue Exemple, 33000 Bordeaux.

We support ourselves from Social Security and pension from a former employer, a total of about €4,549 a month, and hold $185,000 (about €158,798) in savings and investments. The enclosed statement of resources and bank statements show the details.

Neither of us will carry out any professional activity in France during our stay, as stated in the enclosed signed declarations.

We enclose the documents listed below and remain available for any further information you may need.

- Passport
- Passport photos (35 x 45 mm)
- France-Visas application form, signed
- Proof of accommodation in France
- Bank statements for the last three months
- Health insurance certificate covering the full stay
- Birth certificate, apostilled
- Signed declarations not to work, one for each of us (attestations sur l'honneur)
- Statement of resources

Yours faithfully,
[signature] Jordan Ellis
[signature] Sam Ellis

no-work-declaration.title: Declaration not to work
no-work-declaration.text:
# Attestation sur l'honneur

Je soussigné(e), Jordan Ellis, né(e) le 12 avril 1958 à North Carolina, USA, de nationalité américaine, titulaire du passeport n° X0000000,

déclare sur l'honneur n'exercer aucune activité professionnelle en France pendant toute la durée de mon séjour sous couvert d'un visa de long séjour « visiteur ».

Fait à Asheville, le 12 septembre 2026.
[signature] Signature

---
## Translation
I, the undersigned, Jordan Ellis, born on 12 April 1958 in North Carolina, USA, a US national, holder of passport no. X0000000,

declare on my honour that I will not carry out any professional activity in France throughout my stay on a long-stay « visiteur » visa.

Signed at Asheville, on 12 September 2026.
